newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel expects to sell Union Bank holding soon.
newsitem.headline: Israel expects to sell Union Bank holding soon.

text.p: The head of the Israeli government company charged with selling the government's bank shares said on Tuesday he was wrapping up a deal for the sale of the state's remaining shares in Union Bank of Israel.
"We are at the final stages of concluding the deal," Meir Jacobson, managing director of M.I. Holdings, told Reuters.

He declined to give details but the Maariv newspaper said M.I. Holdings had agreed on a deal under which 23.15 percent of Union Bank's shares would be sold to an investor group headed by Israeli businessman Shlomo Eliahu.
The group will pay about $40 million, which values the bank at about $172 million, or book value.

The investment group has a 60 percent stake in the bank, which it acquired from the government and Bank Leumi in May 1993 based on a valuation of $137.5 million. Leumi, which once controlled Union, still holds 16.8 percent.
A source close to the negotiations said he expected the sale to go ahead within several weeks once a share allocation plan had been arranged for Union Bank employees.
Union was one of the banks in which the government acquired shares as part of a bailout of bank shareholders after the 1983 stock market crash.
